title.narrative: Les mandants burundais mettent en œuvre des politiques et mesures intégrées et cohérentes pour des transitions justes

description.narrative:
In the wake of devastating El Niño-induced floods in 2024, which displaced thousands and destroyed homes, livelihoods, and infrastructure, Burundi faces an urgent need to rebuild with resilience. The Government, in collaboration with international partners, conducted a Post-Disaster Needs Assessment to identify recovery priorities. This Country Programme Outcome supports national efforts to link disaster recovery with long-term economic transformation through the creation of decent and sustainable jobs.
The ILO works with the Government and development partners to promote inclusive employment strategies that target vulnerable groups—particularly women and youth—who were hardest hit by the crisis. The programme strengthens institutional capacities to integrate climate adaptation into employment policies and enhances systems for labour market information and skills development, particularly in high-potential sectors like agriculture.
Building on the Global Flagship Programme on Social Protection Floors and leveraging resources from the Regular Budget Supplementary Account, the CPO fosters synergies with the World Bank, European Union, United Nations, and others to ensure coordinated recovery efforts. It emphasizes peacebuilding, social inclusion, and economic resilience in a fragile socio-economic context, aligning with national and international development frameworks. By bridging immediate recovery with sustainable development, the programme contributes to long-term stability and decent work in Burundi.
